full_judgment:
12. The question of citizenship cropped up as a new one because after the liberation war of Bangladesh the question of residence of some persons came for consideration on the presumption that they worked against the interest of liberation war in collaboration with Pakistan which was a foe at that time. Some of them came up before this Court. The similar conflict has been decided by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh specially in the case of Mirza Shahab Ispahani vs Bangladesh, 40 DLR (AD) 116 also in the case of Bangladesh vs Professor Golam Azam, reported in 46 D LR (AD) 192. In those two cases the question as to dispute of citizenship has been decided very precisely and elaborately, finally and effectively considering all the relevant laws and available decisions on the subject of other courts of this subcontinent. 

 Ordinarily, it is for the plaintiff to prove the facts on which his prayer for relief is based. But if the plaintiffs are able to prove that they were citizens of India when they left for Pakistan there will be a presumption that they continued to be citizens in 1953 when they returned, citizenship does not evaporate with the passing of time. It clings to a person wherever he may roam it cannot be taken away from him unless he voluntarily renounces it or is guilty of some conduct involving loss of citizenship. Thus, onus of proving that a citizen of India has lost his citizenship is on the party seeking to deprive him of his rights as a citizen."
